name: Tomb of Thieu Tri
kicker: The only tomb that faces northwest
summary: Xương Lăng, the only Nguyễn tomb that faces northwest, sits among rice fields and orchards about 8 km from the citadel, with the Perfume River in front and no outer wall. Walk the tomb and its temple, set side by side rather than on one axis, and the Đức Hinh pavilion on its low hill. Go for a royal tomb in open farmland.
getThere: About 8 km from the citadel to Cư Chánh, Thủy Bằng, by bicycle or taxi.
heroCaption: The gate framing the hall at Thieu Tri’s tomb

notice.body: Thieu Tri has its own adult ticket, 50,000 VND, and a child from 7 to 12 enters free. The four-site ticket does not include it.

body: Xương Lăng is the only Nguyễn tomb turned northwest. The centre places it in làng Cư Chánh, xã Thủy Bằng, huyện Hương Thủy, about 8 km from the citadel. Chằm mountain is the screen about 8 km in front. The Perfume River is the open path in front of the tomb. There is no outer wall. The rice fields and orchards are the wall.

Thiệu Trị did not build a tomb in his lifetime. After he died, the main works were finished in about three months, and Tự Đức came to check the site on 14 June 1848. The tomb and the temple sit side by side, not on one axis. Đức Hinh pavilion stands on a low hill, and the temple area is about 100 metres to its left.
An adult ticket is 50,000 VND, and children under 13 enter free.

gettingThere: The tomb is about 8 km from the citadel, in Cư Chánh village, Thủy Bằng, Hương Thủy. Go by bicycle or taxi from the south bank.

legs.heading: From the south bank
legs.body: About 8 km toward Hương Thủy, by bicycle or taxi.
